mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a tighter monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to Federal Reserve rate hikes, causing a decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 4.0%), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor market is exceptionally strong (PAYEMS > 158,000) and the federal funds rate is at or above 5.0%, it indicates a high risk of persistent inflation and delayed rate cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both PAYEMS > 158000 and FEDFUNDS >= 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by strong GDP growth), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 thousand units signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% YoY AND HOUST < 1200
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 growth > 2.5% YoY and HOUST < 1200, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive monetary policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising for 3 months), a high federal funds rate compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising for 3 months, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
